newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rangebound as dollar rise capped at 2.5250.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rangebound as dollar rise capped at 2.5250.

text.p: The ringgit was rangebound throughout Asian trading as the dollar's rise was again capped at 2.5250, the level at which Bank Negara Malaysia intervened on Friday, dealers said.
They said the dollar's failure to break through the 2.5250 level could bring it back down to around 2.5200 though the downside may be limited by the strength in dollar/majors.

"Given the dollar/majors firmness, dollar/ringgit should again test 2.5250. But the question is whether the market is ready to push it above the 2.5250 level," said a dealer with a European bank in Kuala Lumpur.
Dealers said dollar gains have been capped by fears of central bank intervention. There was continued talk of Bank Negara palcing orders to sell the dollar at 2.5250, they said.
Bank Negara intervened on Friday to sell an estimated $100 million to support the ringgit at 2.5250 a dollar after a heavy attack on the local currency.
Dealers said the market was also questioning whether Bank Negara will aggressively defend that level especially in the face of a generally firmer dollar.

"We believe that, with the knowledge of the previous intervention level, the market is not that overly long on dollar/ringgit and is probably well prepared to turn short on any signs of a Bank Negara intervention," said research house MMS International in its market commentary.

"Thus, rather than aggressively intervene, Bank Negara is seen putting up a token resistance at 2.5250. Bank Negara may prefer a much more effective intervention at a slightly higher level where it can catch the market long," it said.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5246/50 to a dollar. It closed at 2.5245/55 in Kuala Lumpur on Monday.
